left.heading: WHAT IT IS:
left.body: A tunnel built on the same TLS your browser already uses, running in userspace.
left.draw: A browser window showing a green padlock and the text `https://`, with a globe tilted behind its right edge.

right.heading: WHY IT SURVIVES:
right.body: It can sit on TCP 443 and become almost indistinguishable from normal web traffic.
right.draw: A hand-drawn cloud labelled `TCP 443` with a green ticked shield in front of it and a server stack behind.

how.heading: HOW IT WORKS
how.subtitle: Four design decisions that define the protocol.

cards.heading: TLS UNDERNEATH
cards.body: The tunnel is established with the same handshake your browser performs, through OpenSSL or mbedTLS.
cards.draw: A browser window with a green padlock, an orange beam labelled `TLS` running from it into the mouth of a stone tunnel.

cards.heading: CERTIFICATES AND USERS
cards.body: Full X.509 identity, optional username and password, and revocation lists for taking access away.
cards.draw: A certificate headed `X.509` with a ribbon seal, beside a list headed `REVOKED LIST` with `user2` struck through in red, and a user avatar above.

cards.heading: RUNS IN USERSPACE
cards.body: It is an ordinary program, not kernel code. Easy to port and sandbox, slower than a kernel datapath.
cards.draw: A box labelled `APPLICATION (OPENVPN)` above a dashed line, a box labelled `KERNEL` below it, and two envelopes crossing the line between them.

cards.heading: ANY TRANSPORT, ANY PORT
cards.body: UDP or TCP, on whichever port you choose, including 443 where it blends into HTTPS.
cards.draw: A cartoon parcel labelled `PACKET` wearing sunglasses, walking confidently past a guard booth labelled `FILTER` with its barrier raised.

costs.heading: WHAT IT COSTS YOU
costs.subtitle: The price of all that flexibility.

cards.heading: A LARGE ATTACK SURFACE
cards.body: Hundreds of thousands of lines once the TLS library is counted. More to audit and more to patch.
cards.draw: A tall stack of paper labelled `OPENVPN + TLS LIB` with a magnifying glass resting against its side.

cards.heading: SLOWER
cards.body: Userspace processing and per-packet overhead leave it measurably behind kernel datapaths on throughput and latency.
cards.draw: Two horizontal bars, a short one labelled `OPENVPN (USERSPACE)` and a longer one labelled `KERNEL DATAPATH`, with a stopwatch beside them.

cards.heading: EASY TO MISCONFIGURE
cards.body: A wide configuration surface and negotiated ciphers mean weak setups are entirely possible.
cards.draw: A numbered config file headed `client.conf` with three of its twelve lines struck through in red, and a large question mark beside it.

cards.heading: TCP OVER TCP
cards.body: Running it on TCP for stealth stacks one retransmission scheme on another and collapses under packet loss.
cards.draw: A wide pipe labelled `TCP` with a narrower pipe labelled `TCP` inside it, the inner one knotted and tangled at the far end, envelopes spilling out.
